DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 with FP4 KV caching, reducing its global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token. articles.headline: How to Formalize All of Mathematics
articles.blurb: It would be a terrible waste of resources to spend millions of dollars to formalize mathematics results in libraries nobody uses. Doing so could also disincentivize good research and productive use of AI, disrupt the social norms and practices research depends on, and set the field back decades. Several projects are now working to ensure formal libraries fulfill the community's mathematical goals. Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. This will significantly extend their ability to develop and discover new mathematics.

articles.headline: We discovered something totally unexpected about the neural structure of consciousness

This finding makes it possible to understand how a pattern of neural activity accesses consciousness. There are clear signals that correspond to both what is and isn't conscious. The difference is how each team understands what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA shapes this a lot.

articles.headline: Decoherence
articles.blurb: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.

articles.headline: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)?
articles.blurb: Large language models have demonstrated remarkable abilities in generating mathematical proofs. This could lead to a golden age where a new generation of scientists is empowered, new STEM expertise is developed, and an open, collaborative, and intellectually independent scientific enterprise is preserved. However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.

articles.headline: Why One of the World's Greatest Mathematicians Is on a ‘War Footing'

OpenAI's recent finding in the mathematical field has left him feeling used, as he previously had a good relationship with many employees at the company. Now, he sees them as only using math to evaluate their models, and can't see a way to constructively engage. Despite OpenAI's releases, most problems at the frontiers of math are unsolved, and as math remains infinite, the difficulty of problems is boundless.

There are four types of feedback: positive, constructive, negative, and appreciation. Negative comments can be reframed by acknowledging emotions, separating self from work, and staying curious.

articles.headline: Design in the material you ship
articles.blurb: Digital designers should understand code as a material in the same way architects understand stone or steel, learning what it can do without necessarily mastering how to write it. AI increasingly handles implementation, making it practical to design and review working interfaces in code where responsive behavior, real data, loading states, accessibility, and failure conditions can be experienced rather than represented as static pictures. The valuable skill is therefore shifting from syntax toward understanding how software behaves, testing its limits, and judging whether the resulting product actually works for people.

articles.headline: Synthetic Users vs. Human Respondents: Same Conclusion, Less Variation
articles.blurb: A comparison of 120 synthetic respondents with 604 humans produced the same broad conclusion about terminology for UX work, but AI-generated responses showed dramatically less variation. Synthetic participants converged on roughly a dozen labels while humans produced more than 50, demonstrating a form of mode collapse that can erase unusual perspectives and differences between groups. Synthetic users may help generate hypotheses or identify broad patterns, but they cannot replace human research when unexpected responses, minority perspectives, or natural variation matter.

Tonka provides an organic wordmark, while New Atten, seven colors named after prairie flora, and an abstract mark that can read as a butterfly, flower, or cloud give the system its distinctive character. The mark can frame photography, become a repeating pattern, or function independently, allowing the identity to extend across the website, signage, campaigns, posters, and museum store.

articles.headline: Together gives Clusia a four-petal mark showing AI and people at work
articles.blurb: Together created Clusia's identity around a four-petal mark representing multiple people and AI systems working together inside the assurance platform, deliberately avoiding the robotic visual language common to AI companies. The petals become pixels in 3D illustrations, animate through product states, and combine with Die Grotesk, Vitruv Text, forest-inspired colors, and candid workplace photography to create a system that feels technological but distinctly human. Generative AI was used to explore illustration forms before they were rebuilt and refined in Cinema 4D, while the product itself uses a restrained version of the identity with green reserved for actions, statuses, and the animated mark.
